analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (28.10.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 +60bps to 7723 (+13% YTD), but 60% of S&P stocks fell, a return to an 'AI vs the rest' regime. SOX rose 3.6%, up a third day in a row. US 10yr at 5.02%, Brent $116, Bitcoin $81k.
Kospi +7%, led by SK Hynix (+11%) on better earnings and a memory shortage expected through 2030.

A market comment cited in the note says the bounce is mainly driven by supply abatement as high-velocity supply and length reduction recede. It says the tape is forcing the issue on whether the bounce turns into a rally as headwinds ease (positioning, valuations, earnings T+1 reactions, financing, rates). Catalysts named are FOMC, Mag 7 earnings and the US mid-term election next week.

SK Hynix reported revenue of 104tr won ($78bn, +328% y/y) vs consensus 98tr won, and operating profit of 88tr won vs consensus 76tr won. It plans to return up to $75bn to investors and has long-term agreements with 14 major customers covering over 50% of 2027-2028 capacity.
Apollo data: revenue per worker and profit margins are rising for the Mag 7 but flat for the S&P 493.

Fed meeting: GS expects the FOMC to skip raising rates today and likely deliver a second hike in December. The key question is how the statement changes the sentence referring to the September hike. GS expects no significant new information from the press conference.

Visa management said consumers have jobs and real wage growth and are spending, with resilience across spending bands, strong travel demand and e-commerce expanding into both discretionary and nondiscretionary categories.

GS Consumer Experiences basket: spending growth on experiences accelerated from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026. GS cites attractive valuations, revisions close to inflecting and positioning not overly crowded. Exposure to higher-income cohorts has insulated the basket from higher fuel costs.
Buybacks: November delivers about 10.1% of yearly buyback spend, the second strongest month after August. YTD repurchase authorizations are $1341bn (+14% y/y).

Analysis of 9 Fed tightening cycles since the early 1980s: equities tend to struggle initially after the first hike but recover quickly, yields rise into the first hike, the curve keeps flattening (especially in larger cycles), and the real trade-weighted USD tends to strengthen into the hike.

GS says global central bankers increasingly cite the AI buildout as an inflation driver through three channels: higher memory prices passing to consumer prices, spillovers to consumer electronics, and higher electricity prices from data center power demand. GS considers the direct and indirect pressure limited.
Speculative trading indicator is in the 80th percentile since 1995, below levels reached in late 2025 and summer 2026, and well below the 2000 and 2021 highs.

market_movers.rationale: SK Hynix rose 11% after revenue and operating profit beat consensus, a $75bn shareholder return plan and long-term supply agreements covering over 50% of 2027-2028 capacity.
Visa management cited resilient consumer spending across spending bands, strong travel demand and e-commerce growth on its earnings call.

sector_views.rationale: Spending growth on experiences accelerated to 6% in Q1 2026 from 1% in Q1 2025. Valuations are attractive, revisions are close to inflecting, positioning is not crowded and higher-income exposure insulates the basket.

earnings_insights: SK Hynix reported revenue of 104tr won ($78bn, +328% y/y) vs consensus of 98tr won, and operating profit of 88tr won vs consensus of 76tr won. The results were reported on 10/28.
Visa management commentary on its earnings call cited resilient consumer spending across spending bands.
Alphabet and Microsoft report today (10/28). Samsung, Amazon and Intel report tomorrow (10/29).

tension_points.bull_case: Supply abatement and reduced length are behind the bounce. Headwinds in positioning, valuations, earnings T+1 reactions, financing and rates may ease or turn into tailwinds, which could turn the bounce into a rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Breadth is narrow, with 60% of S&P stocks lower on the day. The 10yr is at 5.02%, and the FOMC, Mag 7 earnings and the mid-term election are near-term risks.
